## Hypothesis

**The highest growth phase of the 2000–1100 BCE interval is the century 1500–1400 BCE, realized as a sustained two-century growth run spanning 1500–1300 BCE (with 1400–1300 BCE close behind).**

Concretely, ranking the nine centuries (CE −2000 to −1100, CE = BCE × −1) by the primary growth metric — the century-mean of the sanctioned openness-growth measure `pollen_grate_100`:

- **1500–1400 BCE → highest growth.** Mean growth +0.00189 (bootstrap 95% CI [+0.00146, +0.00231], clearly above zero and above the runner-up's CI), 79% of years positive, century max +0.00465 (also the window's single largest annual growth), and the 100-yr smoothed openness rises by +0.98 across the century — the largest openness gain of the whole window.
- **1400–1300 BCE → second (same growth phase).** Mean +0.00111, 78% positive years, openness +0.66. These two are the **only adjacent positive-mean centuries**, forming a sustained multi-century growth run 1500–1300 BCE; a 200-yr centered smooth of the growth curve peaks right inside this run (CE −1374, the 1400–1300 BCE bin).
- **Context around the phase.** Growth is absent or negative elsewhere: the 1600–1500 BCE century is the sharpest decline (mean −0.00301, 0% positive years, openness −1.65); weak negatives in 2000–1900, 1800–1700, 1300–1200, 1200–1100 BCE. So the 1500–1300 BCE run stands out as a genuine peak phase bracketed by stagnation/decline.

**Robustness.** The finding is stable: dropping the lone −1100 edge year, and trimming 50 years off each window edge (100-yr smoothing boundary leakage), both keep 1500–1400 BCE on top; even on the "single-spike" reading (single-year max) 1500–1400 BCE ranks #1 (0.00465). **Corroboration:** the coarse-grained capital Z-indicators (100-yr resolution, corroborative only) peak at 1400–1300 BCE (mean Z ≈ +0.94) and stay elevated to ~1100 BCE, consistent with the openness-led growth phase 1500–1300 BCE with capital intensity following slightly later.

## Workflow note
Windowed CE [−2000, −1100] into nine 100-yr BCE-labeled bins (last bin absorbs −1100, rerun without it); scored each century with mean `pollen_grate_100` (primary, sustained-phase reading) plus century max, positive-year fraction, and `pollen_inter_100` change as diagnostics; ran robustness (drop edge year, trimmed edges, bootstrap CIs, spike-reading rank, 200-yr smooth peak/onset); used capital Z-indicators as a corroborative only. Caveats carried: `pollen_grate_100` taken as given (formula not re-derivable from the file; relative ordering is what matters, magnitude is small ≈ ±0.005); only 48 raw pollen observations sit inside the window so stretches of the curve are interpolated — the century-mean ranking is robust to this, a single-year peak alone would not be; 100-yr smoothing leaks across the window edges (addressed by the trimmed-edge rerun).

payload.hypothesis: The highest growth phase of the 2000-1100 BCE interval is the century 1500-1400 BCE, realized as a sustained two-century run spanning 1500-1300 BCE (1400-1300 BCE close behind); the surrounding centuries show stagnation or decline, with 1600-1500 BCE the sharpest downturn.
